newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA LEV FALLS TO 2,650-2,800 PER DLR AT CLOSE.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA LEV FALLS TO 2,650-2,800 PER DLR AT CLOSE.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev weakened to 2,650-2,800 per dollar at close from the morning's 2,400-2,600, due to a rise in dollar demand on an illiquid interbank market, dealers said.
"Final clients bid for relatively large dollar volumes and the lev's morning gains were erased," one dealer said.
Some banks sold light dollar volumes to boost lev liquidity but overall supply was not large enough to meet demand, traders said.

The central bank might also have bought small volumes today to increase its foreign exchange reserves which fell to $415 million last month, dealers said. Bulgarian National Bank's reserves stood at $518 million at end-December.
Central bank officials were not available for comment.
Today's lev rise from 2,800-3,000 at the previous close was ex[ected to be short-lived due to the ongoing low dollar liquidity of the interbank market, traders said.
"We cannot expect a stable lev in the absence of foreign funding and a working programme for economic stabilisation," another dealer said.

The International Monetary Fund (IMF) will resume talks on crucial aid to pull Bulgaria back from the brink of debt default as soon as an interim government is in place, an IMF official said on Wednesday.
President Petar Stoyanov must appoint an interim cabinet by February 20 whose main role will be to organise early general elections in April. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
